questions.question: Who has written the book "The Theory of Wages"?
questions.solution:
The Theory of Wages wrote by J R Hicks, is a classic microeconomics statement of wage determination in competitive markets.

Other books by Hicks are:

 
• A revision of demand theory
 
• A theory of economic history
 
• A market theory of Money

questions.question: Which of the following decisive battles had established the dominion of the British in India?
questions.solution:

• The **Treaty of Allahabad** was signed after the **Battle of Buxar**.

questions.question: In nuclear reactors, which of the following is used as a moderator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Graphite.**__

 
• Heavy water and Graphite both can be used as a moderator in a nuclear reactor.
 
• The role of the moderator is to slow down the neutrons emitted in fission in a small number of collisions.

Extra Facts:

 
• **Uranium** : It is the fuel most widely used by nuclear plants for nuclear fission.

questions.question: Which organ of the government consists of elected representatives of People?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislature**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Legislature:

 
 
• The legislature is the organ of the government which formulates laws.
 
• Legislature enjoys a very special and important in every democratic state.
 
• It is the assembly of the elected representatives of the people and represents the national public opinion and the power of the people.
 
• In most states, the Legislature consists of the Governor and the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). This means that these states have a unicameral Legislature.
 
• In a few states, there are two houses of the Legislature namely, the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and Legislative council (Vidhan Parishad) besides the Governor. Where there are two Houses, the Legislature, is known as bicameral. 
 
 
 
• *Legislative Assembly:*
 
 
• There is a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) in every State.
 
• It represents the people of the State.
 
• The members of Vidhan Sabha are directly elected by people on the basis of a universal adult franchise.
 
• They are directly elected by all adult citizens registered as voters in the State.
 
 

*From the above, it is clear that the ‘Legislature’ organ of the state refers to the elected representatives of the **People****.*

questions.question: Who gave the concept of ‘Separation of Powers’ related to different forms of governments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Montesquieu.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The concept of separation of powers was given by Montesquieu.
 
• Montesquieu described the separation of political power among a legislature, an executive, and a judiciary.
 
• He wrote that the government is morally obligated to serve people, namely by protecting their natural rights of life, liberty, and property

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** ** **__**Aristotle**__

__
 
• Aristotle was a philosopher as well as the pioneer of human knowledge.
 
• He was famous for his statement that "man is by nature a political animal."
 
• Aristotle conceived of politics as being like an organism rather than like a machine, and as a collection of parts none of which can exist without the others.
 
• He was also the propounder of Realism and was entirely opposed to the world of ideas.
 
• He believed in inculcating the habit of reasoning and critical thinking in students rather than just cramming bookish knowledge.

Plato__ (429–347 BCE)

__
 
• He is one of the most dazzling thinkers in the Western philosophical tradition and one of the most penetrating, wide-ranging, and influential authors in the history of philosophy.
 
• After the death of Socrates, Plato, the most famous of his pupils, carried on much of his former teacher's work and eventually founded his own school, the Academy, in 385 BCE.
 
• He wrote dialogues between Socrates and others that would explore philosophical issues. These dialogues would be used in his school as starting points for discussion.
 
• The Platonic dialogues consist of Socrates asking questions of another and proving, through these questions, that the other person has the wrong idea on the subject.

**Hobbes**__

 
• Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher, considered to be one of the founders of modern political philosophy.
 
• He is best known for his 1651 book Leviathan, in which he expounds on an influential formulation of social contract theory.

questions.question: Which among the following forms a common passage for both the sperms and urine in human males?
questions.solution:
Testicles in human produce sperms and urine are formed in the kidney through filtration of blood.

 
• The sperm arrives first at the ampulla, where secretions from the seminal vesicle are added.
 
• From the ampulla, seminal fluid is propelled forward through the ejaculatory ducts toward the urethra.

The urinary tract is a pathway that includes the:

 
• Kidneys: two bean-shaped organs that filter waste from the blood and produce urine
 
• Ureters: two thin tubes that take pee from the kidney to the bladder
 
• Bladder: a sac that holds pee until it's time to go to the bathroom
 
• Urethra: the tube that carries urine from the bladder out of the body when you pee

questions.question: In November 2017, under the Credit-Linked Subsidy Scheme (CLSS), increase in the carpet area for Middle Income Group II (MIG- II) has been approved. The carpet area for MIG-II will be increased to ______________.
questions.solution:
Under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban, these changes were made:

 
• Under the MIG-I category, the carpet area of the houses has been enhanced from 90 square metre to 120 sq.mts, while under the MIG-II segment; it has been increased to 150 square metre from the current 110 sq.mtr.
 
• For the MIG-I category, a four-percent interest subsidy is provided to the beneficiaries with an annual income of Rs 6-12 lakh on a loan of up to Rs 9 lakh.
 
• Under the MIG-II category, the beneficiaries with an annual income of Rs 12-18 lakh get a three-per cent interest subsidy on a loan of up to Rs 12 lakh.

questions.question: Find the acceleration (in m/s²) produced in a body of mass 3 kg when a force of 6N is applied do it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Force (f)** = mass (m)× acceleration (a)

since,

m = 3 kg

F = 6N

Now F = m x a,

6 = 3 × a

a = 2 m/s²

questions.question: The underground water and the water in rivers, lakes and ponds is also _____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**fresh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Water cycle: The whole process in which water evaporates and falls on the land as rain and later flows back into the sea via rivers is known as the water cycle. 
 
• Most of the water on Earth’s surface is found in seas and oceans and is saline.
 
• Freshwater is found frozen in the ice caps at the two poles (North and South) and on snow-covered mountains.
 
• The underground water and the water in rivers, lakes and ponds, streams, wetlands, and even groundwater are also freshwaters. 
 
• Freshwater is just 3% of all the water on Earth. 
 
• Groundwater waters like Rivers, Ponds, Glaciers, etc. are the major sources of Freshwater.
